newsitem.title: USA: Electric Minds brain drain: staffers leave.
newsitem.headline: Electric Minds brain drain: staffers leave.

text.p: SAN FRANCISCO (Wired) There's been an exodus of founding staff members from the high-profile Internet startup Electric Minds recently and the company had trouble making its payroll this week, sources told Wired News.

The company, which has been attempting to turn community-based Web sites into a commercial enterprise under the guidance of Internet pioneer Howard Rheingold, is "just about broke," said one former employee Wednesday.
The San Francisco-based E-Minds has lost at least seven of its staff of 20, including executive producer Abbe Don, chief technology officer Jim Race, and chief operating officer Randy Haykin.
The news comes at a time when the site is premiering a new conference sponsored by IBM, devoted to the upcoming chess match between Garry Kasparov and Deep Blue.

The site is still very active, with more than 1,000 posts a day. "You can support a company for a little while on venture capital," said the former employee, "but then you've got to figure something else out."
